correctness.rationale: The mean field vanishes because tr(m_t Z)=0, while local Z-dephasing commutes with every ZZ interaction term, giving rho_N=U_N m_t^{tensor N} U_N^*. Pairwise conjugation of X_i contributes one cosine factor per neighbor and all sine terms vanish in the product expectation. Since log(m_t)=alpha_t I+artanh(r_t)X and rho_N is unitarily conjugate to the product state, the many-body entropy difference reduces exactly to that one-site expectation. The fixed-time expansion of cos(2Jt/N)^(N-1) then yields the positive N-scaled limit. Fresh basis enumeration through N=8 reproduced the closed expectation exactly.

final_claim: In the dephasing mean-field Ising model with faithful X-polarized product data, the normalized Umegaki relative entropy from the nonlinear mean-field product is exactly r_t artanh(r_t)[1-cos(2Jt/N)^(N-1)], so for every fixed positive time N times that entropy converges to 2 r_t artanh(r_t) J^2 t^2; hence the general O(N^{-1}) exponent is sharp over the same model class.
